drive: material point, uniaxial STRESS (lateral stretch solved so sigma_xx=0)
why_material_point: cheap, and free of the unresolved FE load-schedule question; the graded FE agrees with this drive to 0.4% so it is the right reference

taylor_note.reasoning: The experiment is a POLYCRYSTAL. A [001] single crystal has a LOWER Taylor factor than a random aggregate, so it should carry LESS stress at the same strain, by roughly M_001/M_random. The [001] curve should therefore sit BELOW the measured polycrystal, near 474 MPa at 17%, not above it.

findings: rho0 alone cannot close the gap. A 100-fold reduction, 25 -> 0.25, moves the 17% stress only from +51.5% to +32.6% against the experiment, and against the Taylor-implied single-crystal target the residual is about +66%.
The sign is wrong, not just the magnitude: a [001] single crystal above a measured polycrystal is the wrong side of the Taylor bound.

So the excess is in the hardening RATE, not the initial density: k1 (storage) and y_c (annihilation) set d(rho)/d(gamma), and the law carries a 1/b prefactor with 1/b = 3497 per micrometer, so hardening is rapid by construction at k1 = 0.3432.

Consequence for the plan: the rho0 screen and the hardening-coefficient fit are NOT independent stages. Holding one constant while varying the other still applies, but the order matters -- k1 and y_c have to move first, then rho0 as the finer adjustment.
not_done: No fit was performed. This is a screen to size the calibration, and the calibration itself belongs on the polycrystal as directed.
